**Rigid** (TDD, debugging): Follow exactly. Don't adapt away discipline.

The skill itself tells you which.

## What was wrong

One test failed:

```
expected: ...adapter: "MultiJson::Adapters::JsonGem"...
     got: ...adapter: "MultiJSON::Adapters::JsonGem"...
```

The recent `bundle update --all` (commit `8ed1e1d`) bumped **multi_json to 1.21.1**, which now exposes its adapter classes under a `MultiJSON` constant alias. So `MultiJson.adapter.name` returns `"MultiJSON::Adapters::JsonGem"`.

## The fix

The source (`lib/jsonrpc/parser.rb:50`) is correct — it reports whatever the library returns. The failing test (`spec/jsonrpc/middleware_spec.rb:258`) had a hardcoded expectation of the old name, so I updated it to `'MultiJSON::Adapters::JsonGem'`. I also confirmed there were no other stale references to the old string in the specs.

One note: this test asserts on the gem's internal class name, which is brittle — it'll break again on any future rename. If you'd like, I can make it match more loosely (e.g. `match(/MultiJSON/i)`) to harden it against future gem bumps.
